course_name_original: Principles and applications of heat exchange processes
course_name_en: Principles and applications of heat exchange processes
prerequisites: good level of proficiency in basic disciplines such as mathematical analysis, physics, and chemistry
strong problem-solving skills and analytical abilities from a physical-mathematical and systemic perspective (system balances and their mathematical formulation, equation solving methodologies)

learning_outcomes.text: Acquisition of fundamental knowledge of heat transfer processes.
Ability to analyze inherent technical issues related to heat transfer.
Ability to apply the fundamental concepts of the disciplines indicated.
Development of a systematic problem-solving technique that includes the ability to assess the importance of numerical computations in the proposed problems.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to concepts related to units of measurement
Notable thermodynamic transformations and their corresponding thermodynamic diagrams
Cycle analysis, with particular emphasis on inverse cycles
General information and definitions of heat exchange
Steady-state conduction with and without heat generation
Forced and natural convection: general information and specific application cases
Wall transmittance and overall heat transfer coefficient
Heat exchangers and sizing analysis using the mean effective temperature difference method
Applications related to heat exchange processes in electronic and industrial equipment

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (oral questions: multiple choice and/or demonstrations)
Oral exam (analysis of laboratory work) for candidates who pass the written exam

assessment_rules: The assessment includes a written exam (80% of the grade) and an oral exam (20% of the grade) if laboratory experiments are performed. The written exam consists of numerical and oral questions. Candidates who pass the written exam are admitted to the oral exam, which focuses on laboratory work. Written assignments are not valid for one year; therefore, laboratory work must be discussed at the interview date scheduled for the written exam. Registration for the written/oral exam is mandatory.
